question.problem:
Find the solution to the inequality $\frac{2-3p}{4}<2p+1.$

The solution is $p$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying both sides by $4:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2-3p}{4} & <2p+1 \\ 4\cdot (\frac{2-3p}{4}) & <4\cdot (2p+1) \\ \cancel{4}\cdot (\frac{2-3p}{\cancel{4}}) & <4\cdot (2p+1) \\ 2-3p & <8p+4\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles. 

Remember, when we divide an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

$$
\begin{aligned}2-3p & <8p+4 \\ 2-3p-8p & <8p+4-8p \\ 2-11p & <4 \\ 2-11p-2 & <4-2 \\ -11p & <2 \\ \frac{-11p}{-11} & \,\,>\,\,\frac{2}{-11} \\ p & >-\frac{2}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $p>-\frac{2}{11}.$
